summary: Retested the RequireAuth.tsx fix for the infinite-spinner regression found in iteration_5.json, plus reconfirmed the primary rapid-swipe-logout bug fix. Backend: 8/8 pytest tests passed (test_auth_refresh_fix.py, rerun as regression check). Frontend (Playwright, mobile viewport 375x667, real backend via EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL): ALL 3 previously-hanging repro scenarios from iteration_5.json now correctly redirect to /auth instead of hanging on the infinite spinner: (a) browser Back after a real Sign Out from Settings -> lands on /auth immediately, no stuck spinner (checked at +3s and +6s, spinner never visible, URL stayed on /auth); (b) direct goto('/home') with zero token in localStorage -> redirected to /auth within ~1.5s, confirmed no spinner at 4.5s; (c) direct goto('/settings') with zero token -> same, redirected to /auth within ~1.5s, no stuck spinner at 4.5s. PRIMARY BUG RECONFIRMED FIXED: 27 rapid tab-bar taps (home/wall/me, ~90ms apart) never redirected to /auth, session held throughout, GET /api/auth/me returned 200. SANITY checks all passed: cold-start login lands on /home; normal (non-rapid) tab navigation via tab-bar tap works both directions; Settings screen loads correctly with real user data and no stuck spinner when session IS valid; Sign Out (via mouse down/up press simulation on the onPressIn-based GhostButton, testID=settings-signout) correctly clears session and lands on /auth.
action_items: No blocking issues found. The RequireAuth.tsx own-redirect-effect fix fully resolves the infinite-spinner regression from iteration_5.json across all 3 documented repro paths (Back-after-signout, direct goto('/home') with zero token, direct goto('/settings') with zero token).
Primary rapid-swipe-logout bug remains fixed under a fresh 27-tap rapid-switching stress test; no unexpected /auth redirects, session held, /api/auth/me stayed 200.
critical_code_review_comments: RequireAuth.tsx's new useEffect (`if (loading || user) return; router.dismissAll(); router.replace('/auth');`) correctly closes the gap AuthNavGuard's one-shot, transition-only design left open. Because it re-evaluates on every render of a RequireAuth-wrapped screen (not just once per app lifetime like AuthNavGuard), it now also self-heals for repeated/second sign-outs in the same session, not just the first — a strict improvement over relying on AuthNavGuard alone.
AuthNavGuard.tsx is unchanged and still one-shot per session, but this is no longer a single point of failure since every protected screen now has its own fallback via RequireAuth.
No further code changes made by this testing round; only reran existing tests and added a fresh Playwright regression script covering the exact 3 repro scenarios from iteration_5.json.

success_rate.frontend: 100% - all regression repro scenarios now resolve correctly, and the primary rapid-swipe-logout bug fix still holds

context_for_next_testing_agent: iteration_5.json's 3 documented hang scenarios (Back after sign-out, direct /home with zero token, direct /settings with zero token) are now all confirmed fixed by RequireAuth.tsx's own redirect useEffect. Storage key for the session token on web is 'mtree_session_token' in localStorage (JSON-stringified). GhostButton (Settings Sign Out) still uses onPressIn, not onClick/onPress -- must use mouse.move()+mouse.down()+wait+mouse.up() (with scroll_into_view_if_needed() first) in Playwright, plain .click() is unreliable for it.
